newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso plunge blessing in disguise - Ramos.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso plunge blessing in disguise - Ramos.

text.p: Repeated speculative attacks which forced an effective devaluation of the Philippine peso this month may have been to the country's advantage, President Fidel Ramos said on Monday.

"The recent speculative attack on the peso may have been a blessing in disguise, because it gave us the opportunity to enhance the competitiveness of the peso," he said in his last state-of-the-nation address.

On July 11, the Philippines gave in to speculative attacks that were eating up its currency reserves and allowed the peso the float in a wider band. It appears to have now stablised after falling close to eight percent against the dollar.
"We paid a small price for the long-term stability and resilience of our economy," Ramos said.

"Not only has...(it) conserved our foreign exchange reserves, it should increase the real incomes of our exporters, tourism-related industries, our farmers and fisherfolk, our heroic overseas workers and their families and other dollar earners."

For the past almost two years, the Philippines had kept an iron grip on the peso that made it one of the world's most stable currencies, hardly moving against the dollar until this month's dramatic plunge.
Ramos conceded there were concerns over the impact on inflation.
"But we are confident that it will remain well within single digit levels, with corresponding price stability."
Ramos said financial sector reforms must focus on the need to keep the current deficit at manageable levels.

He also urged Congress to pass remaining tax reforms and called for the growth of a stable capital market to encourage long-term investor confidence and mobilise efficiently domestic and foreign investment.
